Evn passeth now the diving year
AS Winter GENES with icy see Itred sway,
To wrap his snowy shroud round Summers bier.
The forest paths are lone and dreary now,


No vocal strains amid their depths ale heard,
The timid squirrel leaps from Dough to bough,


While seeks its mes some solitary bird!
The flowers that decked the valleys peaceful bed,
Breathing their fragrance on the Summer air,
Are wilhered now; their lOveliness hath fed
Emblem of mortal toms as irail and fair.
How many hearts like these poor fleeing how'rs
Wore the bright lines of beauty's youthful bloom,
III Ws u awhile mid lifc's enchanting bowers,
Then sunk forgotten in the silent tomb?
The Spring again shall come TO deck their bed,
The vocal choir again shall haunt the grove:
Their songs reach not the chambers OF the dead
They cannot wake again the forms we love.
Thus pass the bright and beautiful away,


Fen as Springs flowers, or Autumn's fading leaf;
They bud, they bloom and blossom; then decay
Exotic plants!-how brilliant and how brief!
Read. then, fond man, in yon sal, lonely ground,
Where the mute marble points toward the sky,
Thy historys sequel: as we gaze around,


Behold how iowly earthly hopes can lie.
Here is ambitions goal, affections bound!


All centre in one group, and minglC here
Within the narrow limits of this mOund,--


And claim the parting tribute of tear!
Oh! were it not for pure religions ray,


To pierce the veil hung darkly DER the tomb,
Who could endure to tread lifG's weary way


No star to guide, no rainbow TO lume!
say, ye vain scolfers at the shrine of Faith,


Whose humble worshippcrs serencly wait,
As for messenger of peace, for death,


How will ye enter the eternal gate?
The Souls proud destiny is far above


Her earthly hopes; they do but perish here,
She springs again to H. hi, and life, and love,


Unchecked by Time or Death in her career!
Then let the bright and beautiful part,


On Hopes gay pinions, to the realms of peace;

text:
Immense Gathering OF the Wings OF New


Jersey


The Wing Convention at Trenton, New Jersey,
on Wednesday last the greatest political assem-
blage of the wings which has ever been collected
together within the borders of that very gallant
State. The day was remarkably fine, and the place
of meetlng-the State-IIouse yard--well adapted
for the assembly Of such an immense multitude,
and there were probably less than eleven thousand
persons on the ground The badges, banners and
smblems Of the delegations from the various coun-
ties were very tasteful, and with the gay summer
dresses Of the numerous ladies who favored the oc
casion with their presence, gave the scene quite an
animated and picturesque character. A remark
able degree of enthusiasm inspired the multitude,
and the feeling which was displayed in the various
routes by which the delegations reached the place
of meeting, was we were told quite unparalleled
in the history of eectioneering within the sober
